title: The Endings Before It
label: ch:sa-ordinals-older-endings
canDo: I can say all ten Sanskrit ordinals, sort them by which of three endings they take, and say why the word for first belongs to none of them.

payoff.summary: Complete SA-R63-all-ten and run prathamaḥ to daśamaḥ, then group the ten by ending and name the one that belongs to no group.
payoff.note: The chapter works OUTWARD from the hole chapter 62 left rather than counting down. Sixth is strange until fourth makes it a pair; third is a third oddity until second makes it a pair; and prathamah can only be recognised as a different KIND of word once nine words of the same kind have gone past. Macdonell prints the join inside each headword, so the grouping is read off a dictionary rather than asserted.
